parfumeria.lead: A perfume and cosmetics store in Belarus: a design system, 450+ screens at three widths, 3D video banners for the home page and a site built from the design.

sections.title: the task
body: The store needed a new design for the whole site: from the home page and catalog to the cart, checkout and account. Most people shop from their phones, so the mobile version is worked out in as much detail as desktop.

sections.title: design system
body: I started with the system: colour and type in variables, a documented component library, badges, product cards in several layouts. Every screen is built only from it, so a change to a component reaches every screen at once.

sections.title: screens
body: 450+ screens at 1440, 768 and 375: catalog by category with filters and sorting, a product page with reviews and back-in-stock alerts, search with suggestions, cart, checkout with courier and pickup, SMS sign-in, account, gift cards, brands, promotions and stores on a map.
Every flow has empty, error, loading and out-of-stock states, so developers never have to invent them.

sections.title: 3D banners
body: For the home page I built video banners in Blender: products from the catalog and a promo code banner, 8–10 second loops at 60 fps that play on every screen. Glass, liquid, cap and label follow the real product, and product banners sit on pastel backgrounds so the product never gets lost.

The frame is wider than the banner, so on an ultrawide monitor and on a phone the product stays on the left and never slides under the header or the text. The first banner is Amouage Love Hibiscus with an embossed monogram on the medallion, followed by an Issey Miyake cream and the HELLO promo code banner.

sections.title: the site from the layout
body: To check the design in a browser, I built the site from my own layout: home, catalog with filters, product page with volume options, cart, sign-in, account and checkout. Every screen is checked against the layout at 1440, 768 and 375.

sections.title: a real catalog
body: The layout and the site are filled with a real assortment, not placeholders. I put together a catalog export from the store’s test site: 951 products, 56 brands, photos, prices and volumes. Products are arranged sensibly: perfumes in perfumery, only that brand on a brand page, a discount only where the catalog has one.

Design system: 121 text styles across three widths.

meeting-rooms.title: Meeting Rooms
meeting-rooms.lead: Internal service for booking meeting rooms across the holding. Two roles, 60+ screens with every state, delivered to spec.

sections.title: two roles
body: An employee picks a room from a filtered list, checks its schedule, creates and edits bookings. “My bookings” shows upcoming, current, finished and cancelled ones.
An admin manages rooms, bookings and equipment and sees the statistics.

sections.title: states and rules
body: Every section has loading, empty, error and all dialogs, including a time conflict while booking. Rules from the spec: rooms are available by the user’s location, working hours are 08:00 to 20:00, in-app notifications, 403 and 404 pages.

sections.title: how the file is built
body: Every screen uses Taiga UI design system components. Frames are named “route · role · state”, so a developer knows from the name which screen it is and who it is for.

mimimibot.lead: A Telegram bot built for a client: it makes Pinterest-style shots with the person’s face. In-bot payments and content the owner edits without a developer.

sections.title: how it works
body: You scroll a carousel of ready-made shots, pick one and tap “Generate this shot”. To get your face in the shot, you upload 3–5 of your photos right in the chat. The first shot is free, then token packs.
Three models, each with its own price in tokens. Separate modes: “Pinterest+” builds a shot from a reference you send, “MAGIC+” gives filters, makeup, hairstyles and edits to a finished shot.

sections.title: a platform, not a bot
body: All content lives in the database: shots and prompts, texts, buttons, pricing. The owner changes them in tables and rebuilds the bot for a new niche without touching code.

sections.title: under the hood
body: I wrote the logic myself: four linked processes: taking the request, the generation queue, payment and delivering the result. Payment through YooKassa, tokens are charged atomically and returned on failure. To those who looked at pricing and didn’t buy, the bot offers a discount on its own.
Three sequential database queries at the start of a dialog became one PostgreSQL function: preparing a reply went from about two seconds to 60 milliseconds.

otrx.lead: Admin panel for a module that automatically validates cost estimate files for nuclear power plant construction: a registry, check cards in every status, rules and roles.

sections.title: the task
body: The module checks OTRX cost estimate files and is built into the corporate document management system. It needed an admin panel: a separate web app where checks are run and rules are configured.

sections.title: the admin panel
body: A document registry, a check card in every status (not run, passed, failed, error, re-check, archived), module analytics, rule and notification settings, users and an “Access denied” screen for those whose role does not let them in.

sections.title: how it went
body: The project changed several times. I built the first version on local components, then moved every screen onto the AIPlan-R design system library. After a meeting with the client I reworked the navigation: a project rail on the left, tabs, modal windows.

food-assistants.title: AI assistants for a distributor
food-assistants.lead: Two bots on one infrastructure: “Andrey” answers clients in the CRM chat, “Sofia” helps warehouse staff and managers.

sections.title: the task
body: Clients wait for a reply in chat, the warehouse searches a large catalogue by hand, managers spend time checking clients and creating deals.

sections.title: the solution
body: “Andrey” understands what a customer wants: find a product, ask about delivery, check a spec or call a manager. It onboards new customers and fills in the CRM lead itself: phone, city, business type. Hard cases go to a live manager.
“Sofia” searches the catalogue for the warehouse and answers questions from the company knowledge base. Access differs by department.

sections.title: the key move
body: The model first works out what the customer needs, and then each intent has its own route. Products are found with a direct SQL query on the catalog and assembled into an answer by code, the price list and standard topics are covered by ready text, and the model answers the rest from the knowledge base. This way the bot answers faster and cheaper.

meg-site.title: MEG
meg-site.lead: Corporate website for an engineering company in the TITAN-2 holding: ten pages, each at three widths: 1440, 834 and 393.

sections.title: the task
body: A website to the client’s spec on real content: section texts, a services deck, ISO and GOST certificates, reviews, including ones from international customers.

sections.title: what was done
body: Home, services with a page for each, about, documents, complaints and appeals, reviews, suppliers, workplace safety assessment, contacts and a maintenance page. Every page in desktop, tablet and phone versions.
The request form follows the spec: service, supplier, site, equipment and deadlines. The suppliers page has a block with nuclear industry procurement resources.

osq.lead: One of the largest food packaging makers in the CIS: a home page with a live news feed, a scroll-animated promo page for the new OctoBox and a portal for wholesale clients.

sections.title: the task
body: OSQ was launching OctoBox, an eight-sided container made of cellulose board. They needed a page that shows the product through scroll animation rather than a wall of text. Along the way we refreshed the home page and built a portal for wholesale clients.

sections.title: what was done
body: The OctoBox promo page: one screen, one message about the product; the composition changes as you scroll.

The client portal: a dashboard with widgets (manager, orders, invoices, surveys), a catalog with search and cart, packaging sections, marketing materials to download, the client company’s staff with access rights.

ai-translator.lead: An AI translator for a legal translation team: documents for international nuclear projects, refining a translation in plain words in a chat. Light and dark themes.

sections.title: the task
body: Translators work with contracts and regulations. They needed an interface where a translation relies on glossaries and a base of regulatory documents from the start, and scans are recognised automatically.

sections.title: the solution
body: A chat interface. Paste text or upload a document, get a translation and refine it in plain words, like “make it more formal”. The source language is detected automatically, you only pick the target one. Alternative translations are one click away.
Two roles: an admin works with translation, history and settings, a linguist with translation and history.

sections.title: the principle
body: Every interface element has to rest on a specific requirement in the spec. That is why I removed the dashboard and manual project selection.

captions: Translating a contract and refining it in chat.

svarnoy52.title: Svarnoy 52
svarnoy52.lead: An online store for welding equipment in Nizhny Novgorod: design, a Tilda build with custom code and the whole catalog moved onto the site.

sections.title: the task
body: The company needed a store holding its whole range, not just a couple of showcases. Later the same owners ordered a second site, Svarprom NN.

sections.title: what I did
body: The full cycle: structure, a Figma layout, graphics in Photoshop, the Tilda build. Where standard blocks fell short, I built with Zero Block and added code.
I exported the client’s product base and moved it onto the site, so the catalog holds all the thousands of items with filters and product pages. Responsive layout, basic SEO, request forms.

sections.title: 2026 redesign
body: A new site layout in Figma: home, catalog, product page, about and contacts, for desktop and phone. It is a concept and has not been moved onto the site yet.
The gallery shows the new layouts first, then the 2025 site.

captions: 2026 redesign: 3D scene for the About block, helmet and welding, loop.

packaging-bots.title: AI bots for a packaging maker
packaging-bots.lead: A bot in the Bitrix24 chat picks packaging from the catalogue, collects the client’s details and keeps the lead in the CRM. A summary of the conversation lands in the card, the knowledge base is checked every night.

sections.title: the task
body: First-line sales took a lot of the managers’ time: first you have to understand what the client packs, and only then pick the packaging.

sections.title: the solution
body: The bot merges the client’s messages, works out the intent and searches the catalogue two ways: by meaning and by name. The reply is a product card: dimensions, material, volume, pieces per pack and per pallet, assembly instructions.

Details are collected in stages: name and phone, then a short form. The profile is written only into empty fields and updates the lead in Bitrix24; once everything is in, the lead moves to a deal. When a person is needed, the chat is handed to a manager.
An hour and a half after the conversation, a summary goes into the lead card as a comment. Knowledge-base files are checked every night, the catalogue syncs with the spreadsheet on a schedule.

lines.text: Lead created in the CRM, a manager will call

pix-bi.lead: PIX BI dashboards for the nuclear industry: a “Contract security” report with five urgency levels and project KPI calculation.

sections.title: contract security
body: The report has six screens and a reference board: overview, detailed report, analytics, contract card, empty state and a reference table.
Contracts fall into five urgency levels: overdue, under 30 days, 30–60, 60–90 and unsecured. A monthly chart breaks obligations down by type: advance return, performance, warranty.

sections.title: ready for handoff
body: The file is ready to hand over: 1200+ text layers on styles, screens on auto layout and linked into a prototype.

ubiray-rf.title: Ubiray.rf
ubiray-rf.lead: A new section for a cleaning marketplace: a user profile with feed, career, photos and videos, at three widths.

sections.title: the task
body: The marketplace was adding a business community: users publish articles and news and run their own profile. The whole section was needed.

sections.title: what I did
body: A profile with a cover, stats and “Message” and “Follow” buttons, four tabs with their own layouts (feed, career, photos, videos), posts in the feed and a contacts block. Responsive at 1440, 1200 and phone.

resort-bot.title: AI bot for a holiday resort
resort-bot.lead: The bot parses the guest’s message, clarifies dates, party and phone, answers questions from documents and creates a deal in the CRM. The manager confirms availability and price.

sections.title: how it works
body: A guest writes in chat, the model understands the intent and parses the phrase into fields: dates, adults, children by age, phone. The bot asks for whatever is missing, and for an infant it checks whether a cradle is needed. Questions about the resort are answered by searching documents.

The lead and deal are created in Bitrix24 through Open Lines, the manager sees the whole conversation and confirms the booking. Groups of seven or more, requests for three bedrooms, corporate events and a plain “book it” go straight to the manager.

sections.title: what it filters out
body: The bot filters out spam and ads itself and politely declines off-topic chats. A file from a guest goes to a person to check.

Do you need a cradle for the baby?

vacation-plan.title: Vacation Planner
vacation-plan.lead: A corporate vacation planning service: a vacation table, settings and three roles. Screens checked on widths up to 3440.

sections.title: what was done
body: Two pages, the vacation plan and settings, for three roles: head admin, local admin and user.

A design system on Taiga UI, component specs for developers and an implementation audit. Tables with frozen columns and double headers for dense data, eight modal variants, a notification popover, design-to-code checks and an acceptance checklist.

lotus.lead: A concept website for an Asian restaurant in five breakpoints: 1440, 1280, 838, 697 and 375. The design is mine, the front end is by Nika.

sections.title: the idea
body: A project we did for ourselves, to take the design all the way to a live site. A dark palette with burgundy, large dish photos and the focus on booking a table.

sections.title: pages
body: Home, About, a menu with “Main”, “Breakfast” and “Bar & wine” tabs and dish cards with nutrition facts, contacts with a map and a call-back form. Every page at five widths.

mail-to-crm.title: Email that sorts itself into the CRM
mail-to-crm.lead: Incoming emails get a type on their own: customer, supplier or spam. Managers no longer sort the mail by hand.

sections.title: the task
body: Requests arrived at a shared mailbox and managers moved them into the CRM by hand. Some emails got lost, some ended up in the wrong funnel.

sections.title: how it works
body: Bitrix24 creates a deal from the email, then the bot steps in: it takes the email text, strips HTML and quotes and hands it to the model. The model answers with one word: customer, supplier or spam. The bot sets the request type and a “processed” mark in the deal, and moves spam to the rejection stage.

tetrasis.title: Tetrasis
tetrasis.lead: An appliance store added bundles. I reworked the product page so you see the whole bundle and what is in it, on desktop and phone.

sections.title: the task
body: A new category appeared in the catalog: appliance bundles. A shopper has to see right away what is in a bundle, what it costs and why it beats buying items separately.

sections.title: what I did
body: A bundle page with its contents and total price, a page for an item from the bundle with a link back, promo badges, a set of action buttons for desktop and mobile and an updated catalog.
For the same store I set up autoposting: news goes out to VK, Telegram and Dzen on schedule, without duplicates.

reckon.lead: An online store for a streetwear brand: monochrome, a monospaced typeface, a lookbook on the home page and a Tilda cart extended with JavaScript.

sections.title: the task
body: The brand wanted a store in its own aesthetic: no usual coloured buttons and banners, the collection photos front and centre.

sections.title: what I did
body: A home page with a lookbook, a product page with size selection, cart and checkout, delivery, an about page, the offer and privacy policy, and a phone version.
I built the cart on Tilda and extended it with JavaScript for the store’s logic.

prof-study.title: TITAN-2 career days
prof-study.lead: A landing page for the holding’s career guidance event for school and university students: how to take part, sponsored education, universities, professions and FAQ.

sections.title: what was done
body: The whole page design: a first screen with the application, steps to take part, a company block, universities, the holding’s professions, reviews from sponsored students, FAQ and contacts. Desktop, tablet and phone versions.

svarprom-nn.title: Svarprom NN
svarprom-nn.lead: A second site for the same owners as Svarnoy 52: its own visual key, the same approach to the catalog.

sections.title: what I did
body: A site fully on Tilda: standard blocks, Zero Block and custom code. A dark blue palette with orange, so it does not repeat Svarnoy 52.
Moved the product catalog, wrote the About texts, collected reviews and reworked the first screen. Responsive for phones.

sections.title: 2026 redesign
body: A new site layout in Figma: home, catalog, product page, about and contacts, for desktop and phone. It is a concept and has not been moved onto the site yet.
The gallery shows the new layouts first, then the 2025 site.

captions: 2026 redesign: 3D model of the ATIG 210PAC welder for the first screen, loop.

art-school.title: AI assistant for an art school
art-school.lead: The student sends a photo of a drawing, the bot finds the teacher’s nearest reference, gives a grade and writes a breakdown: composition, structure, tone, stroke.

sections.title: how it works
body: The drawing is compared with the teacher’s nearest reference work: the bot finds it in the database by image similarity and reviews the deviations.
The feedback is short and uses academic drawing terms. Five criteria and a final grade on a five-point scale come to the student in chat, and every new version gets its own grade.

lines.text: Grade: 3+. Structure: check the ellipse of the jug

brain-search.lead: A local server that searches my knowledge base by meaning. I plug it into my working tools.

sections.title: how it works
body: A Python server talks MCP. The database is SQLite: an FTS5 full-text index and embedding vectors in one file. Embeddings are computed locally, and only the fragments found ever leave the machine.

Search is hybrid: vector similarity and BM25 over the full-text index, merged with Reciprocal Rank Fusion. The index holds about 17,000 fragments: notes, project documents and chat history. Only what changed gets reindexed.

preview.query: what did we decide on the catalog?

salon-booking.title: Online booking for salons and clinics
salon-booking.lead: The bot shows the nearest days and free slots as buttons, books the client and sends a reminder before the visit.
salon-booking.client: freelance · beauty salons and dental clinics

sections.title: how it works
body: The client picks a service, the bot shows the nearest days and free slots as buttons. Once booked, the slot closes for others, and the client gets a reminder before the visit.

team-reports.title: WhatsApp reports into a table
team-reports.lead: Employees post raw material intake in a work WhatsApp group, the bot parses the messages and puts them into a table. Edits and deletions are picked up automatically, and once a month a summary is built.

sections.title: how it works
body: A report arrives as an ordinary message: a surname and lines like “material - weight”. The bot parses them and writes to the table, without replying in the chat. An edited message updates the rows, a deleted one removes them. Once a month the summary adds up the weight for each person.

fitness-bot.title: Fitness bot
fitness-bot.lead: Tracking workouts, measurements and diet: a dish is counted from a photo, with recipes, personal reminders and an evening report.

sections.title: what it does
body: Logs workouts and measurements, counts calories and macros from a photo of a dish, suggests recipes. Questions are answered by a separate trainer and a dietitian. The person sets reminders for themselves, and in the evening a daily report arrives.

dice-bots.title: Telegram mini-game bots
dice-bots.lead: Games on Telegram’s built-in emoji in a group chat: slot, dice, bowling, darts and basketball. The bot counts the day’s wins and sends the admin a prize request.

sections.title: under the hood
body: The player throws the emoji into the chat, the value is rolled on Telegram’s side. The bot waits for the animation to end and replies only to a win. Most wins pay out at once, while for the slot’s triple BAR and the dice’s one it is the third win of the day that counts. The player gets a message, the admin gets a payout request.

media-to-rag.title: Documents into a knowledge base
media-to-rag.lead: Documents from Yandex Disk are picked up automatically, text is extracted from them, split into chunks and loaded into a vector database.

sections.title: how it works
body: New and changed files on Yandex Disk are found by MD5 and picked up automatically. Text is extracted from docx, pdf and txt, split into chunks with context, an embedding is calculated for each, and everything goes into the vector database the assistant answers from. A deleted file disappears from the base too.

ai-console.title: AI Console
ai-console.tagline: all AI services in one window
ai-console.lead: A Windows app that gathers all the computer’s AI setup into one window: the voice assistant, call recording, agents, bots and local models.

sections.title: why
body: The services were scattered across hotkeys, scheduler tasks and scripts. To turn something off before a game or to see what was running, I had to remember where it lived.

sections.title: what’s inside
body: Every service has a status and an on/off button. The office tab shows the agents as characters: who is working, who is waiting for an answer. From here you can also write to an agent, see how much of the limits is used, and open the calendar.

sections.title: how it’s built
body: The console lives in the tray and opens with Ctrl+Alt+P. The interface comes in dark and light themes. It works only on this computer and doesn’t accept commands from other web pages.

ai-office.title: AI Agent Office
ai-office.tagline: a team of agents with a dispatcher
ai-office.lead: A working system where a dispatcher hands out tasks between AI agents, and I work as the director: I set the goal, answer questions and accept the result.

sections.title: the idea
body: The agents multiplied: design, sites, a game, content, study. When each lives in its own chat, the overall picture is lost: who is doing what, who is waiting for an answer, how much of the limits is spent. The office gathers them into one structure with clear roles.

sections.title: how it’s organised
body: The dispatcher takes a task in plain words, decides whose desk it is and issues an assignment with a done criterion. The desks are grouped into departments: studio, game, content, personal. Each has its own zone and rules, and each hands in its work as a one-line result: done, question or failed.
Large assignments run as programs: the dispatcher runs them for weeks and hands the next step to the desk that has freed up.

sections.title: control
body: A board shows who is working, who is waiting for me and how much of the limits is left. A supervisor reminds the dispatcher about a desk that stays silent with an open task. Publishing, money and anything irreversible the agents never do themselves: such steps come to me as a question, including on my phone.

call-recorder.title: Call Recorder
call-recorder.lead: I record a call with one hotkey. A minute after it ends I have a transcript by speaker, the gist of the meeting and the tasks in my knowledge base. Speech recognition runs on my own computer.

sections.title: how it works
body: Recording goes on two tracks: my microphone and the other person’s sound, so the text shows who said what. Transcription runs on the graphics card: 15 seconds of recording are processed in about a second, a twelve-minute call in half a minute.

sections.title: the breakdown
body: After transcription the meeting is broken down: the gist, agreements, tasks. The note goes into the project folder, tasks into the to-do list, and the meeting is marked in the diary. Empty pieces and recording breaks don’t get into the knowledge base.

sections.title: confidentiality
body: For meetings under NDA there is a separate mode: a local model does the breakdown, nothing goes to the cloud, and the result is stored apart from the general knowledge base.

channel-pipeline.title: Telegram Channel Pipeline
channel-pipeline.lead: A system for running my channel: post drafts prepare themselves, I approve or edit them with buttons in a bot, and publishing goes out on schedule. My edits teach the system to write closer to my voice.

sections.title: rubrics
body: Three posts a day: news from design and AI, a practical tip, and “A Day Later” about what I did the day before. News only with a primary source, and posts about work come with real screenshots.

sections.title: how it’s organised
body: The control bot runs in the cloud and doesn’t depend on a computer: it sends a draft with buttons, publishes the approved one in its slot, reminds an hour and 15 minutes before it goes out, and sends a summary in the evening.

Drafts are built in several passes: the author writes, code catches clichés and bureaucratese, the editor corrects by a checklist. Gifs for posts are built from templates in the channel’s style, so the feed looks consistent.

sections.title: learning
body: Every edit is saved as a “was → became” pair, and the next drafts take it into account. A rubric in which ten posts in a row went out without edits can switch to automatic mode.

haiku.title: Haiku
haiku.lead: My own voice assistant instead of Alice. It lives on my home computer, answers by voice within a couple of seconds, remembers conversations and recognises which of us is speaking.

sections.title: why
body: We had Alice at home, and her answers weren’t enough: she doesn’t remember what we talked about yesterday and knows nothing about our affairs. I wanted an assistant that answers fast, doesn’t cost money every month and knows the family’s context.

sections.title: how it works
body: The assistant waits for its name, recognises speech on the graphics card, answers and speaks the answer aloud. It recognises a voice from a sample, so it knows who asked and answers with that person in mind.
Conversations are saved to memory. You can ask what was discussed, ask it to pass something on or set a meeting, and the meeting appears in the calendar on the phone.

sections.title: a speaker without the cloud
body: A separate stage: Yandex Station became the microphone and speaker of Haiku. All the logic stayed on the computer and Yandex’s cloud is not involved: the speaker listens to the room and talks in its voice.

lead-agent.title: Order Search
lead-agent.lead: The agent reads order channels and a freelance exchange, picks the suitable ones and prepares a draft reply. Only a person writes to the client.

sections.title: the task
body: Design and development orders are scattered across dozens of channels. By the time you read the feed, the good ones are gone. We built it together with a developer partner: we both look for orders and wanted to spend less time on it.

sections.title: how it works
body: Every 15 minutes the agent reads the chosen channels and the exchange feed. Ads, vacancies and duplicates are filtered out without the model, and the model scores the rest against our skills. An order scoring 50 or more arrives as a card with a price range from the price list. On a button the agent prepares a draft, and then you mark with buttons what happened: wrote, replied, took it.

sections.title: rules
body: Prices only from the approved price list, cases only from our database. The bot doesn’t write to clients. Button presses are visible to the whole team, so two of us don’t write to the same client.

rag-mentor.title: RAG Mentor
rag-mentor.lead: A mentor for newcomers at a retail chain: answers from the company knowledge base, guides through the first-week programme, trains on work situations. The training specialist sees where the knowledge base had no answer.

sections.title: the task
body: A newcomer in retail needs to get a grip on regulations, assortment and rules quickly in the first weeks. A human mentor is busy, the documents are long. The bot answers right away and only from company materials.

sections.title: how it works
body: Hybrid search: by meaning and by words, aware of the employee’s role, so a storekeeper and a cashier get their own answers. Answers link to documents, off-topic questions are politely declined.

Besides questions there is a first-week programme, short courses with tests and a simulator: the bot plays out a work situation and rates the newcomer’s answer. An IT request can be left right in the chat.

sections.title: training specialist panel
body: If the bot hasn’t found an answer, the question goes to the training specialist. They answer in the panel, the answer becomes part of the knowledge base, and the bot itself writes to those who asked. The same place shows how each newcomer’s onboarding is going.

sections.title: quality
body: The models run on my own computer, so the company’s data goes nowhere. After every change the bot is run against a set of control questions, and the “under the hood” mode shows every step of an answer. From a phone the mentor is available in Telegram with a sign-in code.

saldo.title: Saldo
saldo.lead: A concept of a money app for a self-employed (NPD) freelancer: a mobile app, a product website and a web dashboard. The main number on screen is how much you can spend today without touching the money set aside for tax.

sections.title: the task
body: A self-employed person sees one amount on the card, but part of that money is already not theirs: tax, mandatory payments, a cushion for a slow month. I’m self-employed (NPD) myself, so I built the problem from my own experience: income comes unevenly, client invoices get lost, and you remember the income limit at the end of the year.

sections.title: the solution
body: The main screen calculates “Can spend”: the balance minus the tax reserve, mandatory payments and the cushion contribution. Under the number there is a “how it’s calculated” breakdown, so the number can be trusted.

The rest of the product is built around it: invoices to clients with reminders and a payment page for the client, tax and the 2.4M ₽ yearly limit, an assistant that explains the calculation and drafts a reminder for a client who owes money.

sections.title: design system
body: A separate library: primitives and semantic colours with light and dark modes, spacing, radii, grids, 30 text styles and more than a hundred components and sets with states. Every value in the layouts is bound to a token, and every component has a description. The assistant has its own patterns and its own colour, so its suggestions are not mixed up with data.

sections.title: what’s in the file
body: Mobile app 393×852, product website at 1440, 768 and 375, web dashboard at 1440 and the invoice page the client sees. Screens have states: loading, empty, error, offline. The main flows are linked into a prototype.

tg-assistant.title: Telegram assistant
tg-assistant.tagline: the agent office from the phone
tg-assistant.lead: The bot connects me with the agent office when I’m away from the computer: questions arrive in Telegram with buttons, the answer goes straight to the agent, and the work goes on.

sections.title: why
body: Agents stop when they need my decision. If I’m not at the computer, the work stands for hours. The assistant moves these questions to the phone.

sections.title: what it does
body: A question arrives with answer options as buttons; you can reply with your own text, a voice message or a photo. A request for an action the agent can’t take without me comes with “Allow” and “No” buttons.
You can see the office tasks and screenshots of finished work, and give a new task right from the chat. Replies come formatted: headings, lists and tables read on a phone without being cut off.

sections.title: no noise
body: The bot writes only when it can’t go on without me, and doesn’t repeat the same question more often than once in half an hour.

uni-bot.title: Study Bot
uni-bot.lead: A Telegram bot pulls classes, webinars, assignments and deadlines from the university portal and sends only what is needed right now. It runs without its own server and for free.

sections.title: what it sends
body: In the evening, tomorrow’s classes, if there are any. A link to a webinar shortly before it starts. A reminder about unsubmitted work three days and one day before the deadline, new assignments and tests. Nothing else: the main requirement was “no spam”.

sections.title: menu
body: With buttons you can flip through days and the week, and view deadlines and assignments. Classes are cards with the lesson type and whether the week is odd or even, with buttons for the webinar and the portal under the message.

sections.title: no server
body: The check is started every 15 minutes by a cloud function on a timer, and the “already sent” marks are stored in the repository. When the free minutes on the previous platform ran out, I moved the bot so that it still costs nothing.

garden-td.title: Garden Bogatyrs
garden-td.tagline: art and design of a game for Yandex Games
garden-td.lead: A mobile game for Yandex Games set in a Russian fairy tale: vegetables and berries become heroes and defend the garden. A Figma layout, heroes, enemies, bosses and the Gardener.

sections.title: the game
body: A merge tower defense in a Russian fairy tale: heroes are summoned onto the field, identical ones merge into stronger ones, and between waves you pick spells. Heroes split by suit (Earth, Fire, Water, Charms) and rarity; there are hybrids and chapters with bosses from the tales: Nightingale the Robber, Baba Metelitsa, the Leshy, the Sea Tsar and Koschei.

sections.title: what I did
body: A Figma layout: sign-in and menu, battle, plants and summoning, a design system with components, tokens, buttons, hero cards and the battle HUD. Art: heroes, hybrids, enemies and bosses, the Gardener with looks and weapons, chapter backgrounds, interface icons and textures. Checking the game against the layout screen by screen.

sections.title: what it is made of
body: Heroes, enemies and battle backgrounds are built from Blender 3D renders. The sprites on the sheets are shown at the game's native size, without enlarging.

sections.title: boundaries
body: The game code is written by another team member; here is design and art. The battle shots were taken on a test build with the heroes placed by hand.

prosoft.title: PRO-SOFT
prosoft.lead: A site for a 1C integrator: eight pages, mobile versions, a design system and seven 3D scenes on the first screens. Design and 3D are mine, development is by Nika.

sections.title: task
body: The company had two one-pagers on Tilda. They are being merged into one site about 1C only: moving off UPP, ERP and KA rollout, custom work, support. Its clients are manufacturers and retailers with 50 people or more. A visitor has to see within a minute which of the four jobs is theirs, what happens at each stage and what they pay for, then request a diagnostic.

sections.title: idea
body: The company has one strong idea: you pay for the accepted result of a stage. So the centre of the site is not a banner but a stage ribbon, with term, result and payment condition in one table. Tools replace decoration: “Sound familiar?” with a situation picker, choosing ERP or KA with three questions, a sample diagnostic report, a five-question quiz.

sections.title: 3D
body: You cannot photograph 1C services, and people with laptops explain nothing. So each page gets a model that means something: the company mark on the home page, an old and a new computer for moving off UPP, a monitor with a scanner for the diagnostic, a factory and a truck for ERP, a database with integrations for custom work, a monitor with a headset for support, “4 0 4” with the mark.

Models, light and animation are built in Blender in the company colours: white, dark blue and an orange accent. Each scene is a 10-second loop at 3840 by 1920, with the model on the right and room for the headline on the left.

sections.title: system
body: A design system on variables: colour and type tokens, components, a separate page of tools. The palette comes from the company: blue, dark blue for dark sections, orange as the second accent. Onest for text, IBM Plex Mono for numbers and dates. A grid with no fractions: margins 64, content 1312, rhythm between blocks 96. Mobile screens use their own component variants, not desktop overrides.

sections.title: who did what
body: Design, the design system, the Figma prototype and the 3D scenes are mine. Nika runs the research and builds the site on Next.js and Payload. The site is in approval and in development, data in the samples is illustrative.

svarka-3d.title: Welding: 3D and motion
svarka-3d.lead: 3D graphics for two welding equipment stores: an isometric service centre, a mask with an arc, a film built from the site design and a machine for a first screen.

sections.title: the film
body: For Svarnoy 52 I built a 51-second film from the redesign layout: cutting the old home page, a macro of the seam, site sections on a 3D screen, phones and the About mask. Rendered in Blender, titles and screens in Remotion. Here are three silent fragments.

sections.title: service centre
body: An illustration for the Svarnoy 52 service centre page: a cutaway workshop, a bench with an open machine, a multimeter, a pegboard with tools, a gas cylinder by the window. Rendered in Cycles at 4480×3840 with a transparent background and no people. Light, materials and palette match the About mask.

sections.title: before and after
body: The service centre started as a flat isometric drawing and became a 3D scene. The About mask reached its final form through revisions: the hose, the embossed Svarnoy 52 lettering, the materials.

sections.title: Svarprom NN
body: For the first screen of Svarprom NN I built an ATIG 210PAC machine in Blender from photos in the store's catalog. Three-quarter view, an 8° sway around the vertical axis, light on the display and a glint along the edges. The background is transparent.
